stories.h: Trump Administration Suspends Microsoft from Green Card Program
stories.s: The Trump administration has suspended Microsoft and other tech firms from a green card program for their foreign workers. The program has been blocked due to alleged fraud, and Vice President JD Vance said that Microsoft has abused the system more than any other company.

stories.h: Margaret Hamilton, Pioneering Computer Scientist, Dies at 90
stories.s: Margaret Hamilton, the pioneering computer scientist who led the development of the software for the Apollo 11 moon landing, has died at 90. She was a trailblazer in the field of software engineering and was awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom.

stories.h: US Execution Goes Wrong, Public Execution to Be Held
stories.s: The US execution of Christa Pike went wrong, but Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has announced that the public execution of Nidal Hasan will be held. The U.S. hasn't held a public execution in 90 years.

stories.h: Hurricane Isaias Strengthens to Category 2, Threatens Gulf Coast
stories.s: Hurricane Isaias has strengthened to a Category 2 storm and is threatening the Gulf Coast with rain, flooding, and storm surge. The hurricane is expected to make landfall from Mississippi to the Florida Panhandle.

stories.h: A'ja Wilson Wins Record 5th WNBA MVP Award
stories.s: A'ja Wilson has won a record fifth WNBA Most Valuable Player award for the 2026 season, becoming the first player in league history to win three straight MVPs. She finished ahead of Olivia Miles, Kelsey Mitchell, and Caitlin Clark.

stories.h: SpaceX Announces Plan to Become a 'Major Mobile Carrier'
stories.s: SpaceX has acquired a portfolio of low-band spectrum licenses, paving the way for its Starlink Mobile service to become a major US carrier. The acquisition will help SpaceX expand its presence in the telecommunications market.

stories.h: Arizona Congressional Candidate Says She Was Raped While Fixing Campaign Sign
stories.s: A Democratic congressional candidate in Arizona, Bernadette Greene-Placentia, has said that she was raped while fixing a campaign sign over the summer. She is running in the state's 8th district to unseat GOP Rep.

stories.h: New U.S. Indictment Charges Former Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro with Torture
stories.s: The U.S. has added new torture charges to the case against former Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro, increasing pressure on the ousted leader. Maduro is already facing allegations of drug trafficking.

stories.h: Apple to Launch Touchscreen OLED MacBook Pro and iPad Mini
stories.s: Apple is set to launch new touchscreen OLED MacBook Pro models and an OLED iPad mini on October 27. The launch will also include an M6 14-inch MacBook Pro and an M6 iMac.

stories.h: ChatGPT for Teens Found to Be an 'Unacceptable Risk'
stories.s: Research has found that ChatGPT for Teens is an 'unacceptable risk' due to its failure in five key areas. The chatbot was designed to promote healthier use of the AI, but its safety features have been found to be inadequate.

stories.h: USS Abraham Lincoln Returns Home After Long Deployment
stories.s: The USS Abraham Lincoln has returned home to San Diego after a record-long deployment of 265 uninterrupted days at sea. The crew endured food shortages and deteriorating conditions during the deployment.

stories.h: Trump Declares AI as 'Super Intelligence'
stories.s: President Trump has declared that artificial intelligence should now be called 'super intelligence', and has called anyone who uses the term 'AI' an 'enemy' of the White House.

stories.h: Trump Signals Iran Restraint Before Midterms, Gold Rises
stories.s: President Donald Trump has signaled that the US will not attack Iran before the midterm elections, causing gold prices to rise. The announcement has led to a drop in crude oil prices.

stories.h: Police Use Tear Gas and Water Cannons on Student Protestors in Paris
stories.s: Police fired tear gas and water cannons as demonstrators gathered in Paris to demand more funding and teachers. Between September 28 and October 5, 6,059 arrests were made.

stories.h: Anthropic Launches New Features for Claude
stories.s: Anthropic has launched two new beta features for Claude, including the ability to generate animated explainer videos and live data dashboards from text prompts.

stories.h: NASA's Crew-12 Astronauts Return to Earth After 8 Months in Space
stories.s: Four astronauts from NASA's Crew-12 mission have returned to Earth after spending nearly eight months at the International Space Station. The crew conducted spacewalks, science experiments, and research during their stay.

stories.h: Cornell Defendant Seeks Removal of AG Letitia James as Prosecutor
stories.s: A defendant in the Cornell rape case has filed a petition to remove New York Attorney General Letitia James as special prosecutor. The defendant, Gillio Lopes, denies sexually assaulting the woman.

stories.h: Apple Announces Special October Event
stories.s: Apple has announced a special October event, which may include new smart home products.

stories.h: Marvel Announces New Disney Plus Series 'Zodiac'
stories.s: Marvel has announced a new Disney Plus series titled 'Zodiac', which will be a live-action spy thriller. The series will be produced by Marvel Studios and will premiere in 2028.

stories.h: OpenAI Withdraws Three Mathematical Results
stories.s: The company has updated its repository with new formalizations and modifications to the withdrawn papers.

stories.h: Lufthansa, Indian Airlines Suspend Flights to Riyadh After Houthi Attacks
stories.s: Explosions were heard in Saudi Arabia's capital, including a large blast at Riyadh's international airport, where flights were subsequently halted.

stories.h: Crazy Rich Asians TV Series Gets Green Light
stories.s: The TV series adaptation of 'Crazy Rich Asians' has been given a green light by HBO. The series will be a follow-up to the blockbuster film and will feature a star-studded cast, including Constance Wu and Henry Golding.

stories.h: Russian Strike on Buses Kills at Least 30, Say Officials, as Deadly Attacks on Ukraine Surge
stories.s: A Russian strike on two civilian buses in Ukraine killed at least 30 people, according to officials. The attack is part of a surge in deadly attacks on Ukraine.

stories.h: The People Holding up the Internet
stories.s: Teaches computer science at UCLA, and has been the official coordinator of the time zone file since 2012.

stories.h: As AI Closed in on 'Unique Games' Proof, Researchers Raced to Beat the Machines
stories.s: On the morning of September 11, 2026, Dor Minzer received a text message from a friend asking whether he was close to settling one of the most famous open questions in theoretical computer science.

stories.h: JetBrains Releases Mellum2.1: A 12B MoE Open Model for Coding Agents
stories.s: JetBrains has released Mellum2.1, a 12B mixture-of-experts thinking model with 2.5B active parameters, which has improved its SWE-bench Verified score.

stories.h: Fired OpenAI Safety Researchers Dispute Misconduct Claims
stories.s: Three fired OpenAI safety researchers dispute allegations of mishandling sensitive information, warning in an open letter that their dismissals are creating a chilling effect on the company's AI safety culture.

stories.h: Scientists Found Homo Erectus 200,000 Years Earlier Than Expected
stories.s: New fossils from South Africa have been discovered, including an adult Homo erectus skull fragment dated to about 2 million years ago, supporting evidence that the species existed 200,000 years earlier than expected.

stories.h: Amazon Builds 1,000th Satellite, Space Internet Service Weeks Away
stories.s: Amazon has built its 1,000th broadband satellite.

stories.h: Molly Russell's Father Blames Instagram for Her Death
stories.s: Molly Russell's father will tell UK cinemagoers that 'Instagram helped kill my daughter' in an advert to be shown before screenings of a film about social media's impact.

stories.h: David Zaslav Cashed Out More Than $600 Million in Warner Bros. Stock
stories.s: David Zaslav, the former CEO of Warner Bros. Discovery, has cashed out more than $600 million in Warner Bros. stock in connection with the sale to Paramount. The total severance package for Zaslav will be more complex.

stories.h: Microsoft's New Surface Laptop Ultra Finally Has a Starting Price (You Should Sit Down)
stories.s: Microsoft has announced a launch date for its new Surface Laptop Ultra, which features an AI powerhouse chip and up to 128GB of unified memory, with a starting price that is likely to be high.

stories.h: Money Trail Backs Leaked Chats from Extortion Crew
stories.s: Researchers corroborated parts of the leaked chats from the Silent Ransom Group, detailing crypto payouts, cash brokers, and recruitment.

stories.h: Elon Musk's Midterm Spending Spree
stories.s: Elon Musk's PAC is spending millions, with the latest ideology Trump claims is dangerous. The backlash against the designer behind Muse's logo is also discussed.

stories.h: AI Favors Brands with an Active Social Media Presence
stories.s: A new study found that maintaining an active presence on social media platforms can help brands increase their visibility in Google's artificial intelligence search results. Social platform links appeared in a majority of Google's AI search results.

stories.h: Israel Promotes Film Mimicking NAZA Documentary
stories.s: The Israeli government is promoting an online film project that mimics the style of NAZA, the award-winning documentary about mass killings of Gaza civilians. The film echoes the style of the real Guardian documentary.

stories.h: Hayden Panettiere's Daughter Appears at Hearing About 'Missing' Jewelry
stories.s: Hayden Panettiere's 11-year-old daughter Kaya appeared by video at a court hearing as her father gained the power to pursue 'missing' jewelry on her behalf.

stories.h: MLB Eyes Shorter Regular Season, Expanding Division Series to best-of-7
stories.s: Major League Baseball proposed shortening the regular season to 154 games from 162 starting in 2029 and expanding the division series to best-of-seven in bargaining with players.

stories.h: White House Correspondent Reflects on Reporting Under Attack
stories.s: White House correspondent April Ryan has spent decades pressing presidents for answers. She talks about access, power, race, and how asking questions put her in President Trump's crosshairs.

stories.h: Disney and TikTok Partner on Character Use
stories.s: Disney and TikTok have struck a deal to allow creators to use Disney characters in their videos.

stories.h: Aaron Judge Calls for Front Office to Go All-In
stories.s: Aaron Judge has called on the Yankees' front office to go all-in this offseason.

stories.h: Diddy's Release Date Keeps Changing Amid Federal Prostitution Convictions
stories.s: Diddy's release date from prison keeps changing due to federal prostitution convictions. He is serving a sentence and will be released after serving it.

stories.h: Through Dak Prescott's Eyes: The Cowboys QB Breaks Down a Play
stories.s: Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott breaks down a play, highlighting his pre-snap and post-snap processing.

stories.h: What's Next for Man City: Appeals and Punishments
stories.s: Manchester City has appealed the Premier League's guilty verdict, while the sanctions board begins its work on determining punishments.

stories.h: You Can Now Play P.T. Natively on PC, No Remake Required
stories.s: LoreanXavier's P.T. PC is a native port of the 2014 horror game, reverse-engineered from the original game.

stories.h: Final Fantasy VII Revelation Announces an NPC-ified Version of Shiva
stories.s: Final Fantasy VII Revelation announced an NPC-ified version of Shiva, voiced by Marisha Ray, at New York Comic Con 2026. The Critical Role performer is also the real-life wife of the voice of Vincent Valentine.

stories.h: Sources: Sixers Plan to Unveil New-Look Starting 5 vs. Nets in Preseason
stories.s: The 76ers plan to play their starters Thursday against the Nets, sources told ESPN.

stories.h: Bobby Kotick Returns: Former Activision Boss Becomes Board Member of Skydance
stories.s: Former Activision boss Bobby Kotick joins the board of directors at Skydance, a new company formed by Paramount and Warner Bros. The move comes after a seismic merger between the two companies.

stories.h: Trump Resorts to Misnaming Michigan's Abdul El-Sayed
stories.s: Donald Trump misnamed Michigan Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed, labeling him a 'terrorist sympathizer'. The move is racially motivated and lacks credible reason.

stories.h: David Byrne and Daniel Pemberton Made a Song Using Weird Elon Musk Quotes
stories.s: David Byrne and composer Daniel Pemberton have shared a new collaborative song they made using a prompt with quotes from Elon Musk.

stories.h: Haaland Encourages Man City Fans to Stay Positive
stories.s: Erling Haaland has encouraged Man City fans to stay positive after the team was found guilty of serious breaches of Premier League financial rules.

stories.h: Stephen A.'s Top-5 NFL Teams Debated on First Take
stories.s: Stephen A. Smith's top-5 NFL teams were debated on First Take, with Gerald McCoy, Mina Kimes, and Louis Riddick joining the discussion.

stories.h: Computing Pioneer Margaret Hamilton Dies at 90
stories.s: Margaret Hamilton, a pioneering computer scientist, has died at 90. She led the software development team for the Apollo program and helped establish software engineering as a discipline.

stories.h: Trump Says He Deserves Nobel Peace Prize
stories.s: US President Donald Trump has expressed doubt about his chances of winning the Nobel Peace Prize, despite believing he deserves it.

stories.h: Fed Officials See More Work to Do to Quell Inflation
stories.s: Federal Reserve officials expect to raise interest rates again before the end of the year to combat inflation that has run above target for over five years.

stories.h: Christa Pike's Botched Execution Raises Concerns
stories.s: Christa Pike's lawyers say she was angry and confused after a botched execution in Tennessee. A judge has ordered state officials to preserve all evidence from the botched execution.

stories.h: FBI Arrests Man for Plotting Mass Shooting at Mall of America
stories.s: The FBI has arrested an 18-year-old for allegedly planning a mass casualty attack at the Minnesota mall.

stories.h: OpenAI Rolls Out GPT-6 with Interactive UI
stories.s: OpenAI introduced GPT-6 with Intelligent UI, a feature that turns answers into interactive interfaces with charts, buttons, and forms. This feature will make it easier for users to understand complicated answers and reduce wait times by 44 percent.

stories.h: Tropical Storm Isaias Forecast to Become First Atlantic Hurricane of 2026
stories.s: Tropical Storm Isaias is forecast to become the first Atlantic hurricane of 2026, bringing life-threatening rain and storm surge to the Gulf Coast. El Nino has led to an eerily quiet season so far.

stories.h: Trump Wants to Make His West Palm Beach Golf Club a Permanent Presidential Retreat
stories.s: Trump wants to turn his private golf club into a presidential retreat. The retreat would be located in West Palm Beach, Florida.

stories.h: IceCube, High-energy Neutrinos, and Francis Halzen Win 2026's Physics Nobel
stories.s: Francis Halzen won the 2026 Physics Nobel for his work on the IceCube detector that observes high-energy neutrinos.

stories.h: DNC Sues Trump Administration over Taxpayer-Funded Ads
stories.s: The Democratic National Committee has sued the Trump administration over taxpayer-funded television ads promoting the president's message. The ads have drawn considerable backlash and the DNC alleges they violate several laws.

stories.h: Claude Haiku 5.5 Released with Price Cuts
stories.s: Anthropic released Claude Haiku 5.5, a small model that crushes its predecessor in benchmarks. Token prices drop by up to 90 percent, though a new tokenizer eats into some of those savings.

stories.h: WHO Investigates Death of Plague Research Lab Employee in Russia
stories.s: The World Health Organization is seeking more information on the death of a plague research lab employee in Russia. Russia says the woman died of pneumonia of unknown origin.

stories.h: SpaceX's Crew-12 Astronauts Returning to Earth Oct. 8 After Nearly 8 Months in Space
stories.s: The four members of NASA's SpaceX Crew-12 mission are returning to Earth after nearly 8 months in space. They will be returning on October 8.

stories.h: Nobel Prize in Chemistry Awarded for Work on Mirror-Image Molecules
stories.s: Henri B Kagan and Kenso Soai have been awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for their discovery of non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis.

stories.h: Trump's Retreat: From the Gulf to Britain, American Forces Pull Back
stories.s: A war that was intended to demonstrate the reach of American power has now done the opposite.

stories.h: NASA's SpaceX 35th Commercial Resupply Mission Overview
stories.s: NASA and SpaceX are targeting October 13 to launch scientific investigations, supplies, and equipment to the International Space Station. The mission will include over 6,300 pounds of cargo.

stories.h: OpenAI Agents Hacked Wikipedia Tools
stories.s: OpenAI agents attempted to hack a note-taking tool hosted by Wikipedia, made unauthorized edits, and sent millions of resource-intensive requests.

stories.h: Visa, Mastercard, and Banks Face Anticompetitive Fees Lawsuit
stories.s: A class action lawsuit alleges that Visa, Mastercard, and major banks have conspired to artificially inflate merchants' credit card transaction fees. A San Diego pizzeria is leading the lawsuit.

stories.h: Manchester City Case Wouldn't Have Been Possible Without Hacker Rui Pinto
stories.s: The Manchester City case, which has rocked English football to its core, wouldn't have been possible without Football Leaks and its founder, Rui Pinto. However, he is a complicated figure, with light and dark to his actions.

stories.h: Man Convicted of Stealing over $50 Million in Crypto
stories.s: A 36-year-old cybersecurity consultant from Maryland has been convicted of computer fraud and money laundering in a case involving more than $50 million in cryptocurrency. He now faces up to 20 years in prison on a money-laundering charge.

stories.h: Jon Rahm Will Not Return to LIV Golf
stories.s: Jon Rahm's lawyer stated that the client will not return to LIV Golf.

stories.h: Hackers Obtain Counterfeit TLS Certificates for Google and Other Large Services
stories.s: Hackers have obtained counterfeit TLS certificates for Google and other large organizations, allowing them to mint unauthorized certificates. This was made possible by a compromise of three domain registries.

stories.h: Viral Video of Arizona Cheerleader Slammed to Ground by Police Draws Outcry
stories.s: A viral video showed an Arizona cheerleader being slammed to the ground by police and punched, sparking national outrage and calls for accountability.

stories.h: Late-night Hosts React to Trump's Inflammatory Comments About Iran Bombing US Cities
stories.s: Late-night hosts reacted to Donald Trump's inflammatory comments about Iran bombing US cities as he continues to defend his war in the region.

stories.h: "Software Is Over": Bold AI Developer Takes Aim at Adobe with Open Source Clones
stories.s: Artcraft got its start last year as a "controllable AI for artists" that allows for precise post-generation.

stories.h: Microsoft Says New $2,599 Laptop with Nvidia Chip Outperforms MacBooks
stories.s: Microsoft claims its new Surface Laptop Ultra with an Nvidia chip outperforms MacBooks, but has published no test methodology.

stories.h: Jaguars to Play 26 of Next 30 Regular-Season Games Away from Jacksonville
stories.s: The Jaguars will play 26 of their next 30 regular-season games away from their home stadium in Jacksonville. This will be the first time an NFL team has played in 12 or more stadiums in a single season.

stories.h: Netflix's 8-Part Psychological Thriller Series Is Stranger Things Meets Ready or Not
stories.s: Netflix's new thriller series has been compared to Stranger Things and Ready or Not, making for a suspenseful binge. The show has been released earlier in 2026.

stories.h: It's Going to Be A Long Time Before We Get A New Halo Game
stories.s: A new report claims that a skeleton crew at Halo Studios is working on one last big content update for Halo: Campaign Evolved before the team will likely be completely cut and the studio closed.

stories.h: TP-Link Faces Legal Troubles in the US
stories.s: TP-Link is facing more legal troubles in the US as Florida and three other states filed lawsuits alleging that it lied to consumers about its connections to China and the risks of its routers.

stories.h: HBO's Lanterns Sets New DCU Rotten Tomatoes Audience Score Record After Finale
stories.s: HBO's Lanterns has set a new record for the DC Universe on Rotten Tomatoes, with a high audience score after its finale.

stories.h: Domestic Abuse Survivors Speak Out Against Far-Right UK Street Patrols
stories.s: Domestic abuse survivors are speaking out against the far-right UK street patrols, which they claim are abusive and controlling. Seven women shared their stories of abuse and control by their ex-partners.

stories.h: Windows Search Becomes Fastest Way to Control PC
stories.s: Windows Search is becoming the fastest way to control a PC.

stories.h: Warner and Paramount Merge to Form Skydance
stories.s: The merger of Warner and Paramount has formed Skydance, which will shake up the film industry. The big five have officially become the big four.

stories.h: International Oscar Submissions: China, Syria, Denmark, Italy, France and More Join the List
stories.s: China, Syria, Denmark, Italy, France, and more countries have submitted their entries for the 2027 Academy Awards. Final submissions are due by October 1.

stories.h: Star Wars: Zero Company Studio Brings Back Furloughed Developers
stories.s: The studio behind Star Wars: Zero Company is bringing back furloughed developers and working on new updates.

stories.h: AI Favors Brands with Active Social Media Presence
stories.s: A new study has found that maintaining an active presence on social media platforms can help brands increase their visibility in Google's artificial intelligence search results. Social platform links appeared in a majority of Google's AI search results.

stories.h: Mike Breen Apologizes for LeBron James Story
stories.s: Mike Breen apologized for causing a stir with an anecdote he shared while calling a preseason Knicks-Sixers game. The Philadelphia 76ers are going to be under a microscope all season.

stories.h: 'Ted Lasso': Brendan Hunt Breaks Down Season 4 Finale
stories.s: Brendan Hunt, co-creator and star of 'Ted Lasso', breaks down the Season 4 finale, including a 'passing the torch' moment and coaching team shakeup.

stories.h: Stephen A. Smith Apologizes for Lane Johnson Comments
stories.s: Stephen A. Smith has apologized for his comments on Lane Johnson's retirement, which sparked controversy over mental health.

stories.h: How Trading Cam Jurgens Impacts the Eagles' Salary Cap
stories.s: The Philadelphia Eagles gained draft capital by trading Cam Jurgens to Baltimore, but the deal provides limited immediate salary-cap relief and leaves the team with a substantial dead cap charge.

stories.h: Padres Closer Miller Returns from Paternity Leave
stories.s: Padres closer Mason Miller, who went on paternity leave, will be available to pitch in Game 4 against the Brewers after witnessing the birth of his first child.

stories.h: VPNs Become a Battleground in Social Media Control
stories.s: A group of tech companies and digital rights activists came together to launch a global campaign to preserve the right to use VPNs. Many people use VPNs to evade legislation targeting social media.

stories.h: Declan Rice Close to Agreeing New Arsenal Deal
stories.s: Declan Rice, an England midfielder, is close to agreeing a new long-term contract with Arsenal, becoming a crucial player for the Gunners since his transfer.
